issues.description: Method Stock.take(String): the problem specification (UML) and the provided solution declare Stock.take to return an int (using -1 to indicate failure when the ingredient is missing or out of stock). In the template repository, Stock.take is declared to return boolean. This return-type mismatch between the template (boolean) and both the problem statement and solution (int) will cause compilation or logical errors when students implement SealSaloon (which expects an int return value and checks for -1 to detect insufficient ingredients). Files involved: problem_statement.md (UML: take(String): int), template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (take declared as boolean), solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (take declared as int).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Stock.take method signature and implementation to match the UML and the solution: change the return type from boolean to int. Implement it to return -1 when the named ingredient does not exist or its quantity is less than 1, and otherwise decrement the quantity by one and return the remaining quantity. This preserves the intended contract used by SealSaloon (which checks for -1 to detect failure).
